checks.claim: C1: The original d1 model, X, C_pos inclusion and D1 raw variance are correct, including the white endpoint and near/far and temporal Schur mechanisms, with no covariance change.
checks.reason: Own hand reasoning. Canonical H:homog with d=1 gives Gamma=c|x|^-alpha dx for 0<alpha<1, and at alpha=1 the only locally finite even homogeneous measure is c delta_0. B is separable, so Bochner measurability is unproblematic. C_pos is continuous into B, so C_pos is in X_pos. The row maximum sup_s int_0^1|s-t|^-a dt is 2^a/(1-a), attained at s=1/2, so symmetric Schur gives ||q||_X<=K||psi||_X. Spatially, |<f,Gamma*g>|<=||Gamma_near||_1||f||_2||g||_2+||Gamma_far||_inf||f||_1||g||_1, with ||Gamma_near||_1=2c/(1-alpha) and ||Gamma_far||_inf=c; white uses c||f||_2||g||_2. Hence v is a bounded bilinear form on X, with absolute convergence. The form is applied to signed differences only as an estimate, so no signed control is introduced. For nonnegative nonzero psi, |s-t|^-a>=1 on (0,1)^2 and a positive kernel or c int q_avg^2 give v>0. On C_pos, D1 equals accepted (25) by Tonelli, with the same amplitude and normalization. All objects depend only on the class up to null sigma. Pointwise noise values are never used.

checks.claim: C2: The whole-H1 form D2 and variational rate D3 are feasible under exact X hypotheses, with the correct exponent, closedness, countable core equality, measurability and 0<I<infinity, and they match accepted lambda on C_pos.
checks.reason: Own hand reasoning. ||f||_4^4<=||f||_inf^2||f||_2^2<=2||f'||_2||f||_2^3 gives the honesty bound with exact constant sqrt(2) and exponents 1/2 and 3/2. Scalar Young with exponents 4 and 4/3 gives infinitesimal relative kinetic bound, lower boundedness and shifted H1-norm equivalence, hence closedness on whole H1. No H2 operator or eigenfunction is needed. The rate bound is lambda<=C(||h_near||_2^(2/3)+||h_far||_inf^(1/2)). Since ||h_near||_2<=C||q_sigma||_2 and ||h_far||_inf<=C||q_sigma||_1 lie in L2(sigma), lambda is integrable and I<infinity. The Rayleigh functional is H1-continuous, and normalizing a countable H1-dense subset of real C_c^infinity gives a set dense in the L2-unit sphere of H1, fixed independently of psi and sigma. It computes the supremum exactly, so lambda is measurable as a countable supremum of measurable pairings. Positivity: q_sigma>=q_avg gives h_sigma>=Gamma*q_avg, which is nonzero with finite local mass m on [-D,D]. Trial chi(x/R) with R>=max(1,D,2A/m) gives a uniform a.e.-sigma lower bound, so I>0 without continuity of the rough potential. On C_pos, accepted E1<=-eps<0 from nonseparable (3)-(4) and T4.12 at n=1 give sup=-E1. The real positive p_sigma lies in H1 and attains the complex infimum, so the real D3 supremum equals lambda_sigma^2 and max(0,.) is inactive.

checks.claim: C3: A1 is valid for each fixed psi in X_pos through positive cutoffs and mollification, with X convergence, v continuity, core pairings, and diagonal/Fatou giving liminf I_n>=I, under the stated quantifiers.
checks.reason: Own hand reasoning. Truncating min(psi,N)1_{|x|<=N}1_{1/N<t<1-1/N} converges in X by dominated convergence, first for a.e. t in B, then with the L2(t) majorant ||psi_t||_B. Nonnegative space-time mollification with radius below 1/(2N) stays in C_pos for large N. On common compact support, spacetime L2 convergence controls both the L2L1 and L2L2 parts, so both X components converge without renormalization. The pairing int h_sigma f^2=int|sigma-t|^-a int psi_t(Gamma*f^2)dxdt is linear and bounded from L2L1 to L2(sigma) with constant K||Gamma*f^2||_inf, including white. A diagonal a.e. subsequence over the countable core gives liminf lambda_n^2>=each core term, hence >=lambda^2 at a.e. sigma, and Fatou gives the integrated lower bound with no uncountable sup-integral interchange. Passing first to a subsequence realizing the liminf yields the claim for the original sequence too, so the target's allowed chosen subsequence is also sufficient. Growing support is harmless because each psi_n is fixed before its own time limit in accepted (24). No uniform stochastic constants or n(delta) are used.

checks.claim: C4: The A2 inequality and sup equality (A3) follow for the same canonical Q2 and existing real V_c^pos from accepted (24),(31),(32), by fixed smooth scores only.
checks.reason: Own hand reasoning against the accepted consumer. Q2 and kappa in the target are exactly those of (24). Applying (24) to each fixed psi_n and taking the liminf, using v_n->v and A1, gives Q2>=2I-v/2 with no rough stochastic observable. For c>0, cI_psi-v_psi/2<=liminf(cI_n-v_n/2)<=V_c^pos, which gives bounded-above real score sets and one inequality before any supremum over X_pos is taken. V_c^pos is real by (31). Inclusion C_pos in X_pos plus C2 score equality gives the reverse inequality, and nonemptiness is immediate. No optimizer attainment, sup/time interchange or first-mean/Jensen identity enters. Label homogeneity transfers only through equality of already defined values.

checks.claim: C5: O is explicitly defined, rho=g^2 lies in X_pos, the square map H1->B is continuous, and bounded nonnegative w with nonzero product is legal, without proxy or source-identification claims.
checks.reason: Own hand reasoning. ||f^2-g^2||_1<=||f-g||_2||f+g||_2 and ||f^2-g^2||_2<=||f-g||_inf||f+g||_2, with the Sobolev bound, give continuity, so strong measurability transfers by composition. For normalized g, ||rho_s||_1=1 and ||rho_s||_2^2=int g^4<=2||g'||_2, which is correct with the stated nonsharp constant. Then ||rho||_X^2<=2+4 int||g'||_2 ds<=2+4 sqrt(T_g), the time Cauchy-Schwarz step. rho is nonnegative and nonzero since ||rho_s||_1=1 a.e. For w, the product stays strongly measurable and bounded in X, and it is nonzero exactly when w is nonzero on a positive-measure set. Times with w=0 cause no issue because D1/D3 are evaluated for the actual product with no renormalization. Noncompact spatial support is allowed. O contains all constant-time unit-H1 profiles and is the measurable finite-energy class, matching source-normalization adjudication item 5. The target expressly disclaims all-printed-Ad identification, source gradient penalty, kernel choice and optimizer constant maps.

checks.claim: C6: The falsification controls are arithmetically exact, the Riesz control refutes only L2-topology continuity, the code is fully specified and the JSON matches.
checks.reason: Hand reasoning only; I did not execute the script. Riesz: a=alpha=1/2 is legal. int int|s-t|^-1/2=8/3 and the interval self-energy is (8/3)R^(3/2) at R=n^8, so v=(8/3)^2 n^-10 n^12=(64/9)n^2. L2 squared is n^-2 and mass is n^3. The growing X norm means the sequence does not contradict X continuity, and v<=C||psi||_X^2 is consistent, so it refutes only L2-topology continuity, not X density or any SPDE claim. White: time self-energy is (8/3)ell^(3/2), giving raw (8/3)(n/(n+1))^3, and dividing the test by ell gives cost/ell^2=(8/3)(n+1)/n. I hand-recomputed all 5 Riesz rows and all 6 white rows, the key names and the scope string, and they agree with the deterministic script and JSON. Whether the JSON is the output of a run is not established by this review. The controls draw no physical ground-rate or optimizer conclusion.

minor: Label collision: the sup-equality display carries label (A3) inside the section titled A2, while the occupation inclusion section is also titled A3. The phrase 'A1-A3 apply to rho_g' is therefore ambiguous. Renaming would improve clarity; the mathematics is unaffected.

Literal wording 'COUNTABLE H1-dense normalized' core: a normalized set cannot be dense in whole H1. The correct object is the normalization of a countable H1-dense real C_c^infinity subset, dense in the L2-unit sphere of H1.
The target's 0<alpha<=1 should be read as Riesz only for 0<alpha<1 and white at alpha=1, as in canonical H:homog. The near-L1 statement is false for |x|^-1, but that kernel is not in the model.
Bochner classes need a stated jointly measurable representative when forming D1 and pointwise nonnegativity. This is standard, but the proof should say it once and show class independence.

The target and honesty note give no mechanism for I_psi>0. The accepted smooth argument at nonseparable (3) cites bounded continuous U_avg, while rough white U_avg=c q_avg need not be continuous. The same trial works using only nonzero finite local mass of Gamma*q_avg, and the proof should use that form rather than cite (3) directly.
Real D3 versus the complexified accepted spectral statement: the proof should note that real p_sigma attains the bottom and that E1<0 makes max(0,.) inactive.
